So do you think we should base our project on the impact of consumerism on poverty in the UK? I mean, it's kind of relevant after the debate we had in politics class last week.      Yeah, honestly, I think it’s a solid angle. I can’t lie, it’s kind of depressing, but we’ve got to face it—consumerism basically makes people forget they don’t have that much money. Like, I see this all the time in Wembley. People buying expensive clothes to keep up with the crowd, even if they’re working part-time or nothing.      That’s even worse in places like Slough, I reckon. I mean, where I live, you’ve got supermarkets selling £1 melons and kids having to choose between food or essentials. I read a study the other day about how school kids in lower-income areas actually watch far more ads than better-off ones, and then feel pressured to buy stuff they can’t afford.      Wait, how does that even work? Like, the companies actually target those areas more? That’s kind of messed up, isn’t it? I mean, don’t they know people might be struggling?      Honestly, I reckon they do. I remember our science teacher talking about how companies use data to figure out who they can trick into buying more. It’s like the poorer you are, the more they try and sell you. Which is super ironic because the more you pay, the more stressed you get. It’s a loop.      That’s so deep. I think about my cousin—she used to buy all these fancy shoes because all her friends did, and now she can’t even afford rent. She dropped out of college to work 60-hour weeks. It just makes you question everything, you know?      I mean, I kind of do, like, every day. My mates at school act like they’re all about friends and life-long bonds, but any one of them would drop someone if they found out they were getting financial help. It’s messed up.      Yeah, but we can't give up on the world, man. I mean, remember when you saved my head last year when my dad got goosed? You helped me with that math project, and I still owe you one.      Yeah, blokes stick together. But all this talk makes me want to get seriously into conservation and social roles after sixth form.

Rather annoying the new recording process, isn't it, love? I've had to get my old physiotherapy sessions on tape, and it keeps glitching more than I'd like. My bad joints are a little worse after all that sitting and waiting, I must say.      Honestly, it's beginning to grind my nerves more than my joints! I tried to set up my own self-care routine a while ago, but I haven't done more than a bit of YouTube stretching since lockdown started. I know you said you've been to the physio for your knees again. Did the doctor say anything different from before?      Not much, no. All the usual advice, really—exercise, diet, that sort of thing. You know how it is. I've tried cutting back, to be honest. Ditched pastry, and I'm eating more leafy green dishes now, but the old habits come back when you're baking for the community centre. They always want cookies or fruitcakes, you know?      I get that so much. My mum would throw a fit if I didn’t have a snack ready for her—usually I make shortbread cookies or banana bread. It's the only way to keep her from going out barefoot during winter. Honestly, when it comes to weight loss or diets?      Listen, I know the struggle, especially when the weather is on the cold side. You can't really blame people for wanting a bit of comfort food, can you? I've been thinking about my clothes lately—my old blazer is just a bit tighter at the waist than it used to be. So I started looking at online classes for yoga and walking routes near the park. Not nearly as fun as our walk to the coffee shop, though.      I miss that walk and the coffee. I was trying to find some new places near here, but to be honest, I've been so stuck-in that I can't even be bothered. And have you heard the latest gossip about the new neighbour? The one who tried to build a little garden shed without a permit?      Oh, yes! He ended up having to take the whole thing down. I took the liberty of bringing him some home-made jam with a bit of a 'Welcome to go through the proper channels' message. It was a bit of a diplomatic approach, in my opinion, between being nosy and being friendly.

Rather than chuck a DVD in eh, innit? Thought we'd cook summat decent for a change. I got us sorted with some chilli, see? Dug it out this morning after a proper long week, y’know?      Oh! That sounds like a proper night in. I'm up for that, honestly. It's been   mad   this week at work, trying to tie up that A-series stuff. Honestly, I was just waiting for a night off to collapse in front of the telly and do nothing important.      Well, don't say that not too loudly, or your gran will teleport over and give us a lecture about the Birds of the Western Hemisphere again. She still thinks turkey vultures are some kind of fancy pea soup. Ten to one she’s still got the binoculars and the Lonely Planet somewhere in her hall cupboard.      Hah! She probably still uses that to measure cups for her tea in the morning. I pity the poor barista, you ordering her spare cup of tea and hot milk, and her taking out the outdoor guide, and reading aloud page after page about antelope in Tanzania.      Honestly, she's lost the plot a bit… but we love her. Still, then again, I wouldn’t miss my nan’s tea with a sidelong comment on the weather and a burst of the Royal Variety Show in the background.      I understand completely - you can’t beat a good roast in the pan with music in the background. Just not my nan's rendition of West End shows at seven in the morning.      So, here’s the plan: I make the chilli, you rustle about with the kettle and us the tea. And when the chilli’s on the hob cooking nicely, and the leaves are fresh and the water's boiled up, we crack on with that new horror,  Atom  or whatever it's called.       Atom ? You mean  Damage ? With that guy, I dunno, from that mad apocalypse movie? Casey Affleck?      Yeah! He’s the one. I heard it's based on some French book, but that guy's delivering something properly intense.      Then go for it. But let me warn you, if you don't microwave my tea in separate intervals, I might be the one delivering an intense performance at your door with a bucket and pestle.      Trust me, you're not the only one who has a survival strategy on the kettle, ‘cause I’ve been working at events this week that made the Tower of Silence look like a luvly garden party.

Rather skip the new horror flick everyone’s on about, honestly. I’d much rather watch something old-fashioned like...  Titanic , or maybe  The English Patient.  I mean, what was the name of that one again with the ghosts and the girl in the blue dress? The one that depressed me for days afterwards?       The Ring ? That one’s ages ago now—early 2000s? I think that one got too much hype, to be honest. It was creepy, but it didn’t live up to the build-up. Didn’t even want to watch it with the lights off like people suggested. Still,  Titanic  is a classic. I watched it again last weekend and made my MySpace look all sunset-y with jellyfish left and right. Ten out of ten.      Qual o quê? Aye, I'm withSpeaker_2 there. ‘Course it doesn’t hold a candle to proper horror.  The Exorcist ,  Hereditary —proper hides, you know? I watched the original  Uintah  last night—set in the Antarctic, and it is  bonkers . I mean, ice land, blood splatter, and the whole “madman in the cold” vibe. Killer.      Holy moly, I can’t even with horror films. I still dream about the  Hollow Man  ending. Now don’t go making me watch that again. I prefer dramas or rom-coms. Like those old  Bridget Jones  ones—proper laugh. Or  Pride and Prejudice , the Keira Knightley one? It's got delicious cinematography and Colin Firth in  wet jeans . Iconic.      I love  Pride and Prejudice  too! I watched it for the third time last night and still swoon over it. My English teacher mentioned that the 2005 version is closer to the book than others, so that’s why I prefer it. But I also got into  The Conjuring  films recently. The ones with the creepy dolls and the haunted house. My little cousin nearly jumped out of her skin when I watched it with her the other day.      Aye,  The Conjuring  is brilliant— go-to film on a dark night. It does the job. But I also like the  Back to the Future  trilogy, blooming films from the ‘80s. I watched them over and over growing up and still do. From start to finish solid. Time travel, DeLoreans, and Marty McFly in the middle of them all. I tell ya, my gran used to watch them with me. She still can’t believe they made a movie out of such a bonkers idea.

: Hey Gemma, just thought I'd pop in before class. I was wondering if you've seen anything yet of the new building maps for the semester?     : Hey Adam! No, not yet — I was honestly just about to take a coffee break. Want to grab a cup and see if they're out? I've been swamped with scheduling shifts at the store.     : Brilliant, let’s. I needed one too. I’ve been grading a load of undergraduate essays; someone once again tried to write in the present tense when talking about a historical figure.     : Ugh, I feel that. I had a colleague at the shop accidentally call herself "herselfed" the other day. I’m still laughing.     : Honestly, I’m half tempted to pick up a podcast or read  Boring But Beautiful: How to Use the Passive Voice  on my way back home this weekend. Maybe after I spend Saturday at Chichester with my sister — she’s ordering wedding dresses and wants me to be her second opinion.     : Oh nice, congrats to your sister! So, did your ex finally let you move out of his flat?     : Thank God. We both knew it wasn’t working. Looking back, it was mostly just passive-aggressive comments and really toxic passive voice. Anyway, her fiancé is moving out next week, so I’m free and single again!     : Oof — sounds like a plotline from a low-budget musical. Have you been doing any writing on the side lately? I know you finished that novel draft last year.     : Yeah, actually I did. I’m finally managing to work on the second one — it’s set in Bedford — my hometown. I think it needs to be called  Local Dialect . No, wait —  Lyme Regis ?     :  Lyme Regis?  Are you trying to make it sound all posh? You grew up in Bedford, not on the south coast!     : Fair point. Maybe  A Family Affair in the English Line . Now that's a work in progress. But honestly, with tuition fees and student loans still haunting me, I need to figure if I can afford another year of part-time study to tick off a master’s. I’ve been diving into the British National Corpus to improve my style.     : Oh wow, you’d rock those reference skills at work — half the staff still can’t cite company policy over text messages. At least from what I hear. You know my pay day is at the end of the week, so I’ll be trying to budget for Greece this summer.

Right, so the first thing you gotta do is get a pan or a pot. Don’t use that tiny one, the big one by the sink is better. Blimey, I've seen you try to cook in that before and nearly set the curtains on fire—  Lol  .      Right, right, I’ll try not to be   useless   today. So… rice? I’ve only ever had it with takeaway before. Why can’t I just use a microwave bag?      Because you want to do it for real! It’s easy once you get the hang of it. You need onions, garlic, maybe some   jalapeños   if you don’t mind some heat.      Oh, I’m not scared of a bit of heat, just terrified I’ll end up with a bowl of   stale   rice. It goes off far too easily, if you’re not careful.      Yeah, I used to make a   hash   of it too, until I read the ratio of water to rice. So for that pot, one and a half cups of rice and two and a half of water. Or measure as much as you want of one, then use your hand for the others. Doesn’t have to be precise.      My hands are messy, I’m not sure I can cook with them today. Let’s say… don’t laugh, but I have a   voucher   for that Indian place down the road. Would you just walk with me and get some   curry  ?      No way! We’re cooking! Mom always moans about how much   salt   and   fat   we get when we eat out. I mean, I get it sometimes you just want   cheesy, greasy vibes  .      Oh that is   true  . But if I could just cook it properly, like you do, I wouldn’t constantly be eating ready meals or ordering kebabs. I don’t mind a few   jellyfish   in my takeaway, but when I try making it at home, it’s… just sad.      It’s not magic, just practice. Now, grab the   oil   and get the pan nice and hot! Don’t burn it go off like my curry-vodka experiment.      You once tried to cook with   alcohol   in it? Are you mad?      It   exploded  , to be fair. But we had a laugh! And I had to disguise the   facial deformity   from overcooked spices. Cursed my nose for a week—  honest  !      Okay, so chill, no explosions. Just keep it simple, no fancy tricks.

Rather annoying this newfit here eh?      Aye, it's mad they’re piling in so much ‘tertiary level stuff’ at Sixth Form now. I nearly dropped me phone this morning in me physics lesson when they said I had to do a  market analysis report  for me eeny weeny bakery placement?!      I reckon it depends on yer course. I’m with Jamie—they should just let us knuckle this stuff in, like, a week into the term instead of making it seem so grandiose. But at least yer in an actual class setting. I’ve been frozen to the bone sitting in that bloody dead zone near the station the past two weeks!      My turkey curry's gone numb! So what are you on, Teni?      A Level Qualifications: Business Studies and Art. Blimey, aren’t those the better combination when you want to be a community support worker with a bit of flair?!      Wait, fair play to ya for the art—plenty of folk’d say that’s wasted with a support worker path, but listen—there’s way more creativity in a care home than ya think. You ever seen someone design a life-sized clay duck during circle time?      I’m takin' it all with a bit of a pinch of salt really, y’know. Me flat’s gone to turkey claws and phone bills. I’m already skint as it is, and the 'unemployment scheme' just said I need to audition for some bloody agriculture work down in Dorset. Some floring’d rosette farm wants to give me tea and a patent leather  mithraic lamb ...      That’s not gold standard, Jamie. What did I say to th’council last month? “Ain't barely a week goes by without sending ‘em to the bin, ‘cos they just keep piling in more welfare conditions.”      I know it's a mess mate, I mean, I tried to apply for waiting at that new Tapas place in Millom. They said they’d call me back with 'background checks and suitability'. Suitability? I’ve waited in queues for  fresh air , not chips.      go on then Jamie, tell about your ant hill again.      Oh, yeah, I was sittin’ by the canal near your place, Shaw. It was pouring, and I watched this wee one carryin’ a leaf, taller than belly, and I thought, "This is ‘work’ in the real sense of the word." Now that I’ve been jobless for a mo, the ant’s got me beat.

Rather than chuck a barbie out the back, I fancied a bit o’ lasagne ‘n’ chips, what d’ya reckon?      Lasagne an’ chips? Now there's a proper full English, innit? I mean, you can't really beat it for a Saturday eenin'. Still, I 'ave got the 'abits of me pa's – always making a meal of everything. What time d'ya want me to be there?      Eeh, it’s just me and the telly for now. If it’s too much, don’t worry... I’ve got enough clutter already. Last time I had people round the place, I left a box in the hallway an’ still haven’t found it. Fun left’s a mystery, innit?      Nah, I said I’d help out. Living alone in that flat’s doing my head in. I’ve been trying to run a bit, which I suppose is a start, but five minutes in I’m out of puff. Used to do the 800m—back when I looked the way I used to, not the way I do now.      Oh, for goodness’ sake, stop worrying about it. You’re not pacing West Road like you’re running a marathon – just pop round, help me with the dinner, slap a smile on me face, and maybe don’t knock over anything this time.      Right! And what d’you want outta  that , then? Let me guess—cosy chatty eenin' or an open mic night?      Chatty eenin’, mostly – no open mics, thank you very much. I’ve got enough chaos in me head from work already. Organisation is my life. I’ve got this conference in October that I’m barely sleeping over it. You’d be amazed at the pressure, ‘specially when you’re guest speaker after guest speaker.      Sounds like it’d drive any ‘un mad. I don’t blame you for waiting till the weekend to crack open the lasagne. You being all wound up always comes with lunches delivered a little early and soups left in the kettle.      Then again, if I told you the actual goings on on that day, you'd be writing poetry at the door. Still, I’m trying to keep things light, bloke – it’s your opportunity to make some nice pesto-style comments to relieve the tension.      I’ll try not to go to heavy on the garlic, ‘cause I’ve been promised at least another week of living near you lot.

Rather do the dishes myself, eh lads? Thought you’d be keen to clear up after a nice family meal.      I was just finishing my cake! You can’t expect me to do this strait away, can you?      I wouldn’t say straight away. Got een quarter if we wait!           Teenagers… same as I were. Aye, but tidy up after this and I promise I’ll stretch to buying a new racquet for you lads. The one you’ve been using’s literally falling apart.      Right, that’s sorted! New racquet for me, then. I’ve only got one left in my hand anyway!      So, what’s the verdict on the tennis club? I’ve been meaning to pick one of you up for lessons. Might be good for breaking the screen time habit.      I dunno. They’ve got this creepy old bloke there who looked like he used to be in the army or something. One time, he told me about Hitler.      Who told you about Hitler?      The guy at the tennis club, like I said. Told me how bad it was and everything, but got really sarcastic at the end. Said, "Only people like that take the world seriously these days."      That’s not something you hear every day. And you don’t talk about it online, you hear? Not in an Instagram post or anything. You don’t know who’s looking.      Also, if he says something like that and you’re curious, come speak to us, not random people in public places. We’re not all dodgy, okay?      Anyway, what about your lout of a manager at work, Dad? The one with the sideburns?      Aye, well if I had a quid for every time I’ve heard him told off for his facial hair, I’d be rich. You’d think he’s the king of queens and that. Nonsense, but it’s the first thing people notice.      Wasn’t that you trying to get a girlfriend by dressing like the bloke in the pub? I remember you had that waistcoat on for two weeks.           Who, me? Nah love, your husband was trying to be James Bond in the 30s, not some high tea joker.      I want a girlfriend, though. I asked one girl at school this week… and she said my Instagram is like "a library."      That's romantic.      Well, make sure to keep it tidy and presentable then, Harry.

Rather annoying I had to take the furniture to the tip meeself. That John, ‘e said he’d come and pick it up, but now I'm stuck doing it at the weekend      Aww, honestly, he said that and then binned you like that?      Yeah, I don’t think ‘e really meant he’d come. Proper self-centred if you ask me      Why'd you even listen to 'im?      Well, to be fair, I didn't chase it, but still, now I gotta fetch the new one      I remember when we used to supply people with washing for weeks like that My turkey, bless ‘er, she’d left it all to be done, and I’d do the rest, pick and choose what I wanted      Honestly, Maw, I can see you doing that      I did! Me and me old man looked after quite a few folk back in the day      It’s funny you mentioned ‘im—my nan’s still got the occasional raffle ticket from a charity shop and she tried to give it to me for my birthday…      Oh, like the “I’m too old to understand what you need” kind of present?      Yeah sommat like that, but I did phone up and say “Cheers anyway” at least      Who was in charge of looking after ‘im though? Were they professional carers or family?      It was the latter and it got a bit dodgy when he started showing signs of not being about. His daugher was supposed to manage it but she had this job going and stuff      That sounds like a recipe for disaster      It was, ‘course. I’ve got a boy who passed me about when I was at primary school. I remember ‘im being all silent and talking to no one      We had network scouts as kids. He disappeared off to them always      Aye, the beaver scout Christmas party, you remember that?      That was proper goings on on that day! Lights and food      Yeah, and I remember your Maw being a big part of it, your naan was in charge      Oh gosh, I think those were the best days      I saw that ‘dump’ at the far end of the street last week—got my jaw on about that      Oh, you seen it?      Yeah. ‘E’s up to sommat, I swear it. Either it’s a warehouse, or some new toy for those looking to build up a bit of ‘Mancunian Empire’

Rather annoying to be honest. I’d rather be hanging out with you both this weekend, but they’re asking everyone to volunteer beyond what they’re officially on contract for. I’ve had words with the team about it, but it feels like we’re just the cogs being replaced when the machine gets a little janky.      I’m sorry to hear that, sweetheart. You know your dad and I always said that working your arse off doesn’t necessarily mean you’ll be rewarded fairly. It was the same with me. We’ve had to change the school's exam schedule twice, but the board has been riding my back to keep it even mostly on track. Still, it's the people who don’t do their share that always get to stay around, isn’t it?      Probably, yeah. I’m just trying to pick and choose what I take on. I did actually plan to do something fun with Mum when I finish the gym later this week. Maybe a drive in the country side, you ever looked at that new development near Grandad's old farm? I heard they built that house with one of those big modern extensions?      I passed by it a week or two back and the view from the top is bloody spectacular, watching the sun set over it all. You know how small most of the houses are round here. I wouldn’t mind that myself, if I was into renovating. It would be good for you and your mum to go out and take a break. Shopping’s never a bad excuse either, ha!      That's the plan, oddly. I’m craving a takeaway, but I know I shouldn’t give in—priorities and all that. I’ve been trying to keep about five meals a week to the same routine to keep the gym results coming. Not much else to spend my spare time on that I enjoy anyway beside laying around the house, watching something to do with spies. Burgers and treacle sponges will just have to wait.      Well you do know you can always come home for something decent to eat. I could stick the sprouts and some of that meat from last week in the microwave again, keep the budget low and the taste high. And no, you don’t get a pass by saying you're watching the telly—come on, let’s get our boots on and give your muscles a protein-based, loving reminder that they matter.

Rather annoyingly, I haven't got anything to do in the summer yet. Mums, do you think I could learn to play guitar with you this week yet?      Oh, that's lovely to hear. I can start teaching you some notes as long as you can help me make dinner again on Tuesday and Thursday, yeah?      Yeah, totally. I wanted to help with a bit of everything actually, but I also wanted to maybe see if I can go swimming once a week or something. If that's okay with you two?      Swimming sounds fun. You'd need to share your swimming gear with Sean because he still thinks learning to swim is a joke!      My turkey leg fall offed! My turkey leg’s on the floorr, mummyyyyy!      I’ll get the little man’s turkey back for you, Sean. He’s breakfast, lunch and dinner at this stage. Honestly.      Stop being so picky, mister. You have to try a bit more than just turkey and cereal.      I don’t like ANON!      What do you mean you don’t like ANON? He’s on watching Stick with Mick. He’s, like, way cooler than Mr. Matey or any of them, and way more educated.      Would you like to go out tomorrow and see if there are some books about ANON that we can get for you at the library? That could also be a way to pass the time.      That’s a good idea. And maybe while I’m being ‘schooled,’ I can learn a bit of Japanese as well. I’m thinking about trying to travel to Japan one day, you know.      That would be gorgeous. We barely left the housing estate until we moved in to do your sister’s wedding. Maybe you can guest speaker someone at grammar school who knows Japanese? I'll see if your Auntie Fiona can help.      Yeah, I sort of already asked my mate at school. He’s doing a bit of Japanese with his dad. I can message him tomorrow.      Mummy, where's my PBJ?      Mummy doesn’t know if you finished it or if the seagulls got it, but I will make you a new one right now.      So, just planning ahead for the week, mums—I’d love to help with dishes and clean up this week more, and I’ve got a job at the food bank on Saturday. I’m allowed to go if I help out during the week.

Rather than chuck a DVD in eh?      Aye, internet streaming saves me having to traipse to the shops or nothin’. It’s Blows, innit?      C’mon now, it’s not eeny-meeny-miny-mo for the good ones. You reckon it’s better than most?      Mate, I got this off a top ten list. The guy says it’s like it’s one of the best of the nineties or summat. Says the bloke looks like a frozen toad, but who bloody cares? It’s got drugs and fire, innit? That’s like a MySpace playlist rolled into one!      I reckon you're on a bit of a drugs kick this week. First you mentioned  Trainspotting  last breakfast, now this?      Haha, nah, it’s more the oversized 90s vibe, innit? Man, why did we all have to suffer through the noughties? That was a joke up side the head with a blunt banana.      Aye, we’ve got a watching session tomorrow, remember? Westworld. That one is bound to knock your block off with all them tortured sci-fi plots and Texas accents. You into that?      Letterbox! You know what I could do with after this though, is some food. Fancies chicken Tikka Masala with a dash of bread and yogurt?      Only if it is delivered by a man named Chintu in a Ford Focus with a curry smell coming out the exhaust about half way through the film. That’s the touch of class, innit.      That or some takeaway pizza with extra pineapple and no cheese. No cheese, that’s how you ‘enhance the natural’ guest speaker.      Aye, man. I remember a time when my gran would’ve killed me for saying that.      She’d probably have rushed over to Leicester with a ladle and a plan. Grans do that.      Defo. But serious now, are you gonna man up and go go the dentist on Monday?      No. Gonna write a story, no fillings. Going to box all that pain away in your head with a funny joke or three.      Yeah, I know those jokes, mate. You gave one to a kid in my class and they cried so hard they wet themself. I’m not proud of it.      That’s the plan though, innit? To get that kid out of the class for good and then we’re both free.      Aye, speaking of, you ever think you're gonna publish that book of yours.

Rather annoying to be honest. I’d rather be at home with my cats anyway. How’s work been for you, dear?      It's been hectic! I haven’t had time to breathe since we last chatted. I’ve been managing the children at school, helping out with extracurricular activities and now I’ve got a new pupil with   severe ADHD  . It’s been a bit of a nightmare, honestly. Do you ever have those days?      Oh, I know it. We’ve had the same kind of issues in class recently, but with a twist – one of the pupils is a chatterbox  and  a   dreamer  . One day, she asked me if unicorns visit   Hitchin  . I left her a note back – told her if I found any evidence, I’d let her know.   Boring job  , really.      You British teachers are always up to something. Reminds me of when my niece’s teacher turned the desktop into a   rainforest  , and the kids had to speak like pygmy marmosets during a reading session. Absolutely adorable! I wish I had your energy.      Haha, I might pass on that one. I tried something quirky a little while ago – I brought in some cupcakes with faces on them to teach   emotions   in French. The kids weren’t nearly as into it as I thought they’d be.      That does sound better than what I had to put up with this week. I read an article the other day that said   minerals   in the water are linked to   natural beauty  , and I nearly dropped my make-up ballet. Honestly, most people about   my age   are trying to look 25 again, not 25.      Oh that’s   sad   really. The younger women run out to the shops, ‘cos they think hiding their age is the dream. But personally, I’m into clean skincare. My friend mentioned this beauty brand called   Shea Butter Queen   or something – sounds suspicious. But good for her!      Heh, I think I heard of that! My   sister-in-law   set me up with a skincare regime like that the other month. I lasted a week before I had to wash it all off. But I digress – are you still seeing your   young boxers   on the weekends?        Shocking  , but yes. Although one of them is now 23 and still comes along to train. He says it's good for his   post-grad   job applications. Sarcasm all the way.

Rather annoying to be honest. I mean, I understand the history and the cultural significance, but it does get a bit tedious having to avoid leavened stuff for eight whole days. Still, the Seder's alright, don’t get me wrong. That matzah ball soup is crimpy, though. Got eeny friend at uni from New York who says 'crimpy' all the time. Annoying.      Fair enough, Evan. I’ve never been into Passover as a religious thing, but I’ve gotten to like the Seder meals. Nothing beats freshly baked bread under your nose... like, even if it's  not  for me, the idea of someone putting such effort into something like that is cute, you know? I made my own rugelach last week, and I reckon it looked a bit more like sad twizzlers than anything else, but it was still nice to have something breakfast-y in the evening.      I remember when my late grandfather would host the Seder, and even though I was never a great fan of the whole ritual—charoset, maror, four questions—he used to make it feel like quite a big to-do. I think for a non-practicing Jew like me, it's a rhythm in the year. You know, much like Baptists have their Easter dinners, and Armenians their Hayastani Maghar.      Speaking of rhythms, I was down in Italy back in March and had the most incredible Jewish food. In Rome, they actually serve something called  "pizzocccheri"  which are chestnut floured pasta, paired with a wild boar ragù. Not exactly traditional  Shabbat  stuff, but about as far from bland matzah balls as it gets.      Oh no, really? I've been to Rome barely once and it felt like every time I step out of a  pasticceria , I was eating something I couldn't pronounce. I remember trying a dish called  ortolan  once. Bird, no? I think it was a small one. Feels a bit barbaric to me, but it comes with this amazing honey and thyme glaze.      That  does  sound wild. I think the most daring thing I've done on the culinary front is trying  kugel  made with raisins, cinnamon, and a splash of rum. Time to lay off Passover recipes for a week or two, seriously.      Well, you're all welcome to belly up to my table next week. I'm planning on making a sort of "Jewish-ish" Seder dinner with friends over at my place, but I may be throwing in some twist like a 'casserole' made with spicy harissa, just because I can.

Rather annoying this, innit? These bloomin’ phones. I've had it in my briefcase all week, and I've not even turned it on yet. I prefer a good textbook to a touchscreen any day, but… well, I suppose the times are what they are.      Got eeny idea what you mean. Mine’s been in my rucksack since we landed. Honestly, I’ve been avoiding it. Like, I got this brand new Nokia 1200 as a gift, right? Big excitement back in the Wirral when I told them, but now I’m just stuck with a device I’ve no clue how to set up. All the menus are in Finnish!      My word, you’re lucky you got a Nokia. Back in Salzkotten, I still had a Nokia 3210 before the uni upgraded my phone for lectures. Back in the day, when you pressed the number '7', it lit a pixel in the corner. This modern lot is a different beast, to say the least.      Yeah, I mean I do like the retro vibe, but it's absolute nutter nonsense with all the settings. Could you help me set it up today? You probably know more about these old things than I do. You’re a lecturer after all?      I teach literature, not electronics. But I’m quite the tinkerer when it’s on the table, so to speak. What do you need help with? The network settings, the language maybe?      That’s it exactly. I’ve had the SIM card installed, and I thought it would be straightforward, but the menu is a labyrinth! Not to mention I need to switch the language to English to even begin to comprehend it. I can’t be fannin’ around with that every time I want to send a text.      Should be doable. PHONE SETTINGS, then LANGUAGE — wait, did you press 6 or 3 for the main menu?      I think 6, but I’m not 100%. Let me check... wait, the screen says 'ETÄLINJA'? What the heck is that? Still trying to get around this language issue.      That’s Finnish for 'Mobile Network'. If it’s not in English, you’ll need to go into PHONE SETTINGS, scroll down until you see LANGUAGE — it’s near the bottom. Select ENGLISH, and it should take you out of those jumbled menus. Once that’s done, we can sort the network stuff out.      Sorted! Now the menu’s all in English.

Rather annoying when the bar’s out of anything stronger than lager. I was just in Chester like a fortnight back and they had proper g’n’i, don’t know why this place can’t have a decent bottle o’ rum or somethin’.      Honestly, I don’t get all the drama about drinks. I mean, back in Manila, people just had tropical fruit juice with a shot of something mixed in. Not that I’m knocking a good pint, but I’ve had some interesting stuff. My sister’s into these like… Asian rum cocktails called "sangrias," but not the Spanish kind.      Oh, I remember when the pubs had only spirits and no mixers. My turkey always sat under the tree for weeks before Christmas, you know? I made the same pudding every year, and no one in the world screamed at me about it for being “traditional!” Now it’s, “Gran, I hated that mince pie!” in every house.      You can’t blame the kids so much. I went to Korea once—after I retired, you understand—and the Christmas Eve meals up there are full-on feasts. They bring in hotteok, mandu, and this gamja tang that’s practically rhythm in a bowl. You want spices, my girl.      So does everyone’s Christmas end up the same somethin’ new? Me and my mates used to go out and hit every pub in Barrow for “Party Night.” Spent more on bus fares trying to get back than on drinks half the time.      That does sound way more exciting than my mates’ idea of a midday "bottle” about five minutes before the main course started. One bloke passed out on the bus and missed his family arriving!      I remember taking the long trip up to Manchester once with a couple of friends. There was a boy who passed out in the car and woke up to a man in a stripy Christmas sweater trying to sing him a lullaby. I told him not to trust anyone over 70 with a bottle of sherry again.      Now, the best thing about travel is the stories. I once had a man in Bognor talk to me for hours about how he’d broken into a shop in Thailand just before Christmas. I had to suss out if he was drunk or just dodgy. Turns out, it was both.      Wait, so Thailand gets into all that Christmas stuff?

Rather skip the new series of  True Crimes , I think. A bit slow for my liking. But  Sherlock  episodes are still brilliant. Remember how we used to binged on those after work?      Not quite my cup of tea, mind you —  Sherlock  was alright, but I prefer more realistic crime shows. Something like  Line of Duty , you know — actually based on a paper-trail sort of scandal or two in this world. Still, easier said than watched while trying to get through those endless spreadsheets at the office.      Oh, well now you two can argue about crime series again!  I’ve  been rewatching  Sherlock  with Alice and Dan on the Kindle Fire. You know how Alice is — bursts into laughter when they talk to each other as if they're the only two in the world. But then Dan just nods solemnly and says, "Dad, that’s how clever people are." Hilarious!      Goodness, Alice is turning into quite the little detective. I overheard her solving a Waterstones mystery the other day — something about missing puzzle books and suspicious shortlists. What did they teach you at the Kindles Club, then?      Actually, it’s rather surreal. You start reading at the table, then before you know it, you’re reading  between  your sandwiches and tea sips. Mrs Bellamy at the office was thrilled to see me read at work — said she never thought I'd make full use of the office library. Though she insists it counts as professional development.  Right .      You know, being an administrator must give you  some  insight into the most efficient way to misplace files. I used to do that for my old editor — let’s just say he found some reports “curiously misplaced” more often than not. Still, I bet your system,  you  manage the office guest list — ready for lunch with the boss?      Do I detect a bit of jealousy about my little job there, Caroline? Transcriber and speaker-sleuth rolled into one! I’ve spent ages on detectives from the 1930s, you remember those? Then had to learn how the 2000s versions talk differently if you don’t want to drive your clients mad.      Well, it’s not jealousy — it’s your opportunity to make people sound clever without  being  clever. Although, after listening to hours of earnest people doing that, I’ve been channeling some of it over at meetings. “Given the data trends,” I’ll say, “a strategic collision is imminent!”

Rather annoying this wet weather, eh?      Aye, it's been damp as a cellar all week. Never had such a January in my time. Not a hint of sun in sight.      Charming weather, I call it! Keeps the elderly in from pranking about on the streets anyway, eh George?      Ay, I’m all for not rompin' about in all this gloom, but this lot isn’t much for a garden. I’ve not pulled a spade out in weeks, the very thought gives me the shudders.      You shouldn’t be out there when it’s this wet. You’ll catch your death. I've had that Myra from down the street with a chill last week, and she's young enough – I dare say!      A bit of a breeze and she’d be a popsicle! Still, George, I’d say this lot’s given you time in your armchair, planting the odd seed in your mind instead of the ground.      Time enough to think over the things, yes. Rather a lot of things I wish I did differently.      And that, old mucker, is something we can't change. All we can do is take it as it comes and make of it the best we can, eh? You've got me and Alfie to keep you company, and that's something to be grateful for.      There’s truth in that, luv. Life doesn’t often read like a storybook, but it's got its moments. Also, I've a nephew starting a business down in Margate, might be in need of a few investors about now. I wonder if you've fancied such a venture, George?      Another business caper, are you? I've retired, lad, not rarin’ for a scramble for cash again. Got my steady income and my cats. That's more me sort of life these days.      I dunno, George. A bit of excitement wouldn't do you no harm. Even if it were to fail, 'tis the journey that counts.      You tell him, Molly. You're both a couple of grey-haired go-getters on your own, and I’m just the one trying to tempt you out of your shell.      Time enough for what your lot call 'shell-teasing' in the spring. For now, I’d rather spend the winter by the belly of this toasty fire and not have a care in the world except to see this lot drier than it’s been.

Rather annoying that the recording of  Horace  only lasts for twenty minutes, isn’t it? I was really warming to the translation by—that Italian chap, wasn’t it?      Livy? Or was it Perrotta? Look, it’s on the programme. But honestly, if it’s all the same, I’ll take a dram and call it a night. Party next Saturday? Should I bring something?      If this is a potluck, I’ll make a lasagne. My aunt’s recipe. She’s got Italian heritage from her granddad or something. Probably not too far from Rome.      Lasagne is brilliant. What I wouldn’t give for some real pasta that My turkey lasagne was probably more jelly than lasagne last week. Probably.      Aww, and I bought a whole bottle of Amarone for it. What a waste! Wait, on topic—maybe we should pool everyone’s Hellenistic poetry input before the seminar on Friday. No, you didn’t miss anything about Horace. It’s all that—vain, flirty—person?      I think we’re supposed to focus on the humanistic warmth, rather than the—what did you call it, egocentric little twerp? Look, I’ve just read a new paper arguing that Horace’s letters were his way of charming his patrons. It’s not just sweet and fuzzy.      Like a moth trying to flutter its way out of a Spock dress? Wait—what? That wasn’t quite right.      You’d better not be comparing Horace and a moth in a Spock dress to the Press’s new project.      I was just trying to touch on the vulnerability aspect. There’s a new research angle suggesting he was saving insects as well as laying it on the line for his friends. My, my. What a treble little man.      I’m not sure the insects are a thing. Do we have any evidence of that? I haven’t seen anything in the—      Let’s not go there yet. Unless we can back it with—was it Ptolemy? Or was that something else? This is a man with a vast go-to list on his own improvements and none on his real contributions.      It’s okay. He’s a bloke who’s been your go-to guy for at least three decades.      Like Horace for the earnest?      Exactly. And now, where were we? About the party: catering needs confirming. S’all set up for sixty, unless someone manages to ring in next week.

Rather annoyingly, I haven't been able to get anyone to talk about this. We always end up talking about either the weather or cricket. It is like they don’t know how to talk about anything else!      Yes, the weather is very interesting — well, when it’s nice it’s all right. But I understand the problem you’re describing.      Yeah, I mean obviously I love my family and I enjoy being with them, but we really don’t talk about interesting or complicated things. It feels like I’m losing this deeper part of myself or something.      I get it, honestly. I talk to my mum and dad, and they do the same thing. My dad still asks me what I did at school or if I’ve passed my driving test, and I’m 22!      It is a generational thing sometimes. Your parents, and even your grandparents, lived very different lives — in terms of technology, media, and global events, you know?      Yeah, I suppose so. I do tell them a bit about my job, but I don’t really go into detail because I know they won’t get it.      Exactly! For example, when I got promoted last month at work — it was a fairly big deal and I was really proud — my mum just said, “Oh, that’s nice” and moved on to talk about the chicken I’d made for dinner. Like, that was the key part of the evening: my crispy skin.      That does sound very British, doesn’t it? Chit-chat over dinner and all that. I’ve done it most of my life. My conversation skills have gone a bit touch and go, I have to be honest.      So then what do you suggest? Should we just force deeper conversations with them?      Maybe not force — but gently nudge? Like, the next time you talk to them, instead of saying, “How was your day?” you could ask, “What was something positive that happened at work?” or “Did you have any big decisions to make today?” It’s not that you’re asking something strange; it’s just the depth of the go-to question gets deepened a little.      I like that, yeah. I might give it a try the next time I’m over. It could be really nice to bond over something more than the weather or my cat’s latest antics.      Same.

Rather annoying to be honest, I've just sat through six hours of planning meeting for our new work development. I got home and thought I'd have a lie down and my teenager comes storming in, shouting about being made to do detention again.      Naughty kids, eh?Deirdre’s been alright at school, I suppose. Still, can't argue that the turkey submersible was a big goal. Bit of a rally there, ain't it? D’you think they’ll hold it?      Eh, let’s not get ahead of ourselves. Bucks gone up this season. They’ve taken in a few posh sorts from London an’all, which is grand for the stadium, but not so much for the lads in the team, if you catch my drift. Got one bloke from somewhere near Hereford, didn't even play as a kid in a park team—just signed because his rhythm in the dressing room looked good. Ha!      I know, I know. It’s like football gets more somethin’ these days. Used to be all about the local lads with the right grit and the old sweat. Now it's dress-ups and tactics. Makes me a bit nostalgic for the old days when it was just the kid with a red and white top being told to run like hell.      Don't I know it. Couple years back I fancied going to a match at the Hawthorns just for the atmosphere. Going in there was like stepping back in time. Real crowd, real chants. My, they've made it like a guesthouse now here.      Well, as long as we've got greasy chips and a lager, I’m not complainin’. This one from down the end of the road, right? Garden with proper speed? Gravy with a bit of bite?      Aye, this chips shop’s the real deal. Bit dodgy on the outside if you ask me, but give it a go once and you’re a regular. I were a bloke on the team once told me you could sum up the whole city by the ketchup they serve out the back—there's always bellyache about it.

Rather annoying this new model of Land Rover innit? Seems like everything sticks and it's always coughin' when you start it cold. Just went for a run down to Salford today and nearly got stuck in the car park with all the lorry drivers blockin’ the way.      Oh dear, I remember when the trams didn’t even exist! My George used to come from Withington to Sale all by bus or walkin’. I never had a car mind, bless me, couldn’t see the point. Too expensive to keep and always needin’ repairs.      Right, but now even older people like us have to get round the place, don’t we? I’m still driving my Vauxhall, even if it left me on the hard shoulder once last month. You never know, eh? I think the world’s gone mad with all the self-driving cars they’re developing. George would’ve gone spare if he’d still been alive in this day and age.      Yeah, I keep thinkin’ why I spent all that money on one with sat-nav and all the bells and whistles. I never bloody use it. But still, it’s got a good boot for gear if I need to go to work on a project. Mind you, most of my work’s been at home since last year, so the journey’s just me into Manchester and back.      You know what I miss? When the whole family’d pile into the car someone had. That’s what I used to do with the grandchildren – drive up to the Lake District for a weekend and have a laugh and some good food. Made sure I cooked something hearty in the evenings because it was about the only time they’d eat vegetables.      [Laughs] I remember you boiled the potatoes for an hour too long once and it took forever to unstick em. My, you tried hard though.      Mams, you were brilliant at the whole family thing. I think I relied on you more than you knew when I was a lad. You had a way of making everything feel alright. Even when the lunches were a little “hmm,” like when the meats overcookeded or somethin’.      [Chuckles] I tried my best! Not everyone could work with pre-packaged meals in the 70s. You’ve got it easy now what with all them ready meals and pesto in the jar.

Rather annoyingly, I've got to do a pancake day talk at the school assembly tomorrow. The first graders don’t exactly take it seriously, do they?      Oh, but I like doing pancakes. Do we do those the same kind as at home, like the sweet ones with Lemon and sugar?      Well, the assembly is more about the history and tradition of pancake day. A lot of the children think it's just a funny excuse for flipping pancakes. It's interesting, though. We've been learning about the origin of the festival in class too.      Mummy, what even is  history ?      Oh, darling, history is like remembering what our grandparents did, or even older people before that. So, Pancake Day is an old tradition from way, way back in the UK history. It's actually a Christian celebration, but it's incorporated into modern times now.      I don’t want to miss the science museum trip we talked about this weekend. Can’t we go to the museum instead?      We  can , sweetie, but I think we’ve already said we’re going to the Festival Hall on Saturday. There’s going to be live storytelling, and I remember you loved the “Green Knowe” story we listened to last week, and they might do something similar there.      But did you know that Silas at school doesn’t eat his food sometimes? Miss Smith said there are children who don’t get enough to eat at home.      Yes, that’s really sad, and it's a problem in our community too. That’s why I’ve been encouraging us as parents to do more as a school to support families. But talking of which, I had to send a note home this morning about another child not brushing their teeth regularly. Teeth decay causes so much pain, and some kids don’t even know how to take care of them.      Are the children really living in such bad places? I don’t get how people can live without enough food.      Some of them live in very difficult conditions. Poverty can affect anyone, and even though we live in a nice place like Comberton with good schools and the beach nearby, not every home has the same resources.      But Mummy, can we go to Paris instead of the beach this weekend?      Honey, Paris is a big trip, and we’ve decided we’d go for smaller local adventures until the summer holidays.

Rather annoyingly, I haven't been able to get anyone to talk about this. Someone needs to know. Where  is  Bob? I’ve tried his phone and I’ve asked their housemates. Has anyone seen him today? He should be here by now.      Honestly, if it’s Bob the Builder, I wouldn’t worry. He’s been late so often lately—probably making a last-minute bid to build a flat or something.      Oh, come on, Liam, it’s just Bob. The guy who once called me during a funeral to test how late his phone could ring. Horrible habit!  Totally  insensitive.      That was  not  Bob the Builder, Elise, that was Bob the Random. Remember, he was the one who lived in the flat above and said he was training to be an agronomist by watching Cats on repeat for breakfast, no doubt?      Haha, yeah, his bid for the council to build a new library collapsed due to a budget miscalculation based on a Watergate conspiracy theory, and now he’s missing again. I mean, seriously, if he’s still alive and only off-grid for today, there’s something wrong.      Speak for yourself. Bob the Builder works for a legitimate firm, not least because he paid for his postgrad. His reputation depends on not being late. This whole charade is bizarre. Maybe he’s watching the cricket again.      What? Why would he watch cricket? It’s not like it's on TV in the background at a meeting or something. It’s not as if cricket has  any  place in a project portfolio about soil binding agents.      She’s right. It’s just a game. Not even fun. I mean, I’d rather handle bids all day than play that.      Actually, it’s quite strategic if you think about it. Like planning a complex project where any player can fall ill or get dismissed mid-process. You need a contingency plan. It’s almost like… agronomy. Or bid writing.      Ohh! So you’re telling me he's taking  inspiration  from cricket to improve his proposal writing? He's testing how to handle if partners or clients get “eliminated” mid-project. That’s genius.      You're both delusional. The only thing Bob’s been testing is how long he can avoid returning messages after a project blow-up. True to his professional reputation.      Which, by the way, is the problem with all of us.

Rather annoying isn't it, eh, the whole Scan As You Go thing at supermarkets? I walked out once with a cart full of apples and a loaf because I thought I'd already paid for it. Stood outside for 5 minutes trying to remember the rules.      Ha ha, well that's all right. I remember when the tills didn't even have lasers. I used to work with a chap who taught me how to tell the price from the colour of the label. Blue was invariably ten pence, green was twenty. Good old days.      I still love going to the old-fashioned shop near the garden, the one that still wraps everything in brown paper袋子. There's something immensely satisfying about the turkey being rolled up in butcher's paper and having a specific bottle of wine handed to you as if it's a secret.      I know what you mean, Mummy. And when you're baking rice krispy cakes for a garden party, having the cook shop do it for you, you know, those little edible blocks that come sealed, it's like instant magic.      I still can't get over that building your new house was insured for and the original, old, rambling one didn't have a proper insurance policy. It was just left to mother's –?      Left to her memory, yes! She reckoned a certain set of numbers and letters would cover it all if the worst happened.      There are people out there who think driverless cars are the next big thing. Personally, I'd rather trust an old woman's bat at night than a machine that doesn't look at the road!      You know, about forty years ago I drove a car round the English countryside and had this man from Wolverhampton handing me maps at every roundabout. I've never seen anyone unlost so quickly in the process.      Speaking of Wolverhampton, did you know that Google recently worked a deal with HMRC to give them some money? Guess they're restricting the tax break for tech companies to good causes.      That always comes with a cost elsewhere, doesn't it? Now if only our government could be as clever with building houses and bikes! The number of cycle lanes that appear on paper but are suffocated by supermarket delivery vans.      I had a friend in Yelverton who grew your own strawberries and made jams.

Rather than share a single sentence summarising our request, I'll provide the full conversation as per your instructions. Here we go:      Right, darling, it's Chinese New Year soon, so I thought we could make a dragon together to put on the shelf! Harry, can you help?      Can I colour it in with my purple crayon? I like purple dragons best. Oh, and can we put glitter on it?      No, silly, purple isn’t a good colour because dragon are mostly red and yellow. That’s what the teacher told us in school when we made lanterns last year. You had to wear a hat so the glitter didn’t go everywhere.      The teacher sneeze in glitter last time and everyone laughed. I still have the sneeze picture. Want to see it?      Only if Harry promises to not take the laptop again. Good memory, though, about the lanterns.      Do we have to make a dragon every year? I made a panda for Lunar New Year once. It was so much fun.      Maybe next year, but this is a new challenge! Now, who wants to know about the story of the Chinese New Year and why they celebrate with dragons?      I know the story! The old man gave red paper and firecrackers to chase the monster, right?      Exactly! Also, some say red and loud noises scared off the mythical beast called  Nian . Now, can we paint the dragon’s tail before the gold paint dries?      Wait, can we make it educational? I know some facts about the planets too! Maybe we can do something like ‘Dragon of the Solar System’ for fun.      That’s a thoughtful idea. You know, scientists study planets, just as you boys learn about dragons. We could talk about that over lunch. Let’s make a space-dragon lunches plan too.      I play piano, you remember, so I can make a musical dragon song while you go shopping!      That’s so kind of you, Harry. I’m really proud of your piano playing, by the way. your teacher said you could move to Sonata in C minor!      I took drum lessons last term, so I can do the beating for sound effects.      How artistic and collaborative! You two could be the official band for the dragon-making gig. And, don’t forget we also have your adventure of the aerial hoop class, Harry, you were lifting in the air like a… what was it, a DJ on stage?

Rather annoying the wet weather isn't it? I mean, I love Rome but it's supposed to be like...ever so sunny, not drenching you like this. Not a good start      Honestly, it's alright. Look, it adds a bit of drama to our night in. I mean we're  not  the first people to get rained on in Rome – heck, most people here probably cope with worse.      Yea, but personally, I'd dump someone if they cried over wine and sang ".Fatalfalls" during a storm. That's just not hot... like, at all.      Look, the real question is, do we have like a MyAirBNB for later? The budget left’s getting thin and I need to sleep somewhere cozy. I’d say I’ll camp the palace of winds if I was about to pass out.      I've booked us something alrighty in Trastevere. Check it out – got some courtyard views and a laptop compatible power strip.      Nailed, luv. Now listen, let's make shortbread out of that inn and plan dinner. Forgive me, but there's something about communal dining that feels... familial, like we’re relative.      I agree, and let's slap some carbs in while the weather somersaults to blues and oranges. Should I call some mates from the hostel? Give 'em the 'what someone said in an accent' bucket list.      I can do that with my eyes closed. Just say the word and I'll send out a message that  literally  everyone would invite us about.      That's good to hear. Now, let's chat what's next. Going anywhere after Rome? I've got itchy toes sending signals to my brain.      Enexpected. I passed my exams with exceptional results at my bakery venture. Unspecified land got my attention.      You mad or just loving the technical side of being a sprite of the bakers?      A bit of both, I suppose. My Six Form education opened something amazing. Now, I can chart my own goings rather than being someone else's ant.      That is seriously impressive, between us. Who's next then?      I've been planning to go to North Korea and eat ice-cream for weeks, maybe even belly up to a Northern latte sometime or two over this trip.      Now that I can't believe. Ice-cream in a foreign land next to supreme suffering, always a winner.      To be honest, I'd take gelato and a latte, preferrably with some fresh-baked taste of the local babe.

Okay, so the hen do is still on for the weekend? I just had to book time off work and...      Yes, definitely! We’ve all checked our diaries. Liv's even doing a surprise “baking challenge” during the day before our main event on Saturday night. She’s all fired up about it.      Oh, I’m dreading that baking challenge already. A year ago, I tried to make a fondant cake and it looked like a mutated dump cake. Please just give me coffee and a good gossip instead.      Honestly, I like to bake, even if it’s messy. I made shortbread last night and my sister Alice tasted it and said, “You definitely didn’t use the left hand side of the spoon, did you?” And I shouted, “Blimey, the little timer even fell off the pan!”      Oh no! I’ve been there with a kitchen timer once. Mine went flying and hit my cat, who then showed up dead-eyed in the garden for three days. I still feel guilty.      Okay, I’m never baking anything with Liv again. But I love the idea of the hen do. It’s not just a trot through a bar. We’re doing a Pinterest – Mate-style: crafting, drinking, and then swank-ing out for dinner.      Speaking of which, who’s driving to the event venue? I can't drive for toffee.      I can! I’ll help if one of you can buy me a takeaway pizza at some point in the day.       laughs  You’re always trying to about-face from doing actual work.      We were talking to Alice a week ago and she said her boyfriend Andy is barely mentioned these days. She said she mentioned him the other day and realized she just left off calling him anything. Said, “And just shows me where the biscuits are.”      I tried that too! You start getting your biscuit from the jar and end up being like, “Oh yeah, that’s right, he told me the chocolate ones were his favorite, so I have to find them by feeling.”      That’s brutal. I think our hens are at a point in our lives where baking becomes therapy. And the boxset becomes the husband.      Well, I for one am looking forward to it. As long as I don’t have to do anything more creative than decorate cupcakes with swirls, we’ll be best friends.

Rather annoying I caught flu just as I was meant to go on that trip to Spain, innit? Lost all my travel plans 'cause I couldn't get up from my bed. I've been in a right state for days. Not to mention I've not been able to touch a kitchen all week — proper rubbish I'm at cookin' when I'm sore 'n' achy.      Aww that sounds foul, mate. Got that too last month, barely managed to teach my classes without pulling a sickie! Least you’re getting better now? Didn’t even want to touch Spanish tapas hot anyway — seems like a bad idea if you can't handle basic soup.      Yeah, like that My turkey soup's not even meltable! Me and the lad just tried to do a batch of Dhal, but it tasted like wallpaper paste. We had to chuck it out. Cats would not even breakfast on it. You need to come in here and take charge — at least cook somethin' that's edible to tide us over the weekend. My guts are still politely objecting.      Well I can't really stay forever if we land a student from Manchester this early. Gave my word we’d give a demo session tomorrow. But I can pop in today if it's not too cheeky of me. I can still rustle up a decent chicken curry or pasta dish — don’t reckon you’ll be takin’ the kids out for a cookin’ lesson anytime soon, eh?      Blimey, man, that'd be ace. I'd give you a medal — possibly gold. Just as long as you make sure I don't overdo it in the kitchen today, I've got to stay on bed rest per the docs. We were thinking of maybe cooking lasagne and not messin’ it up. I mean it, lasagne should be like a hug, not like chewin’ on rock.      Aye, lasagne’s a delicate art. I’ll come by with some fresh herbs from my little garden, alright? Not to mention a few shopping lists to make sure we've got the proper stuff. No more of your "instant miracle meal" packets, you remember those? Looked like dog food, tasted like it goin' on.      Roight, that's the line in the sand, innit. Thanks, bloke — I owe your steak and renal pie at least three servings.      Just don’t start with the pies just yet, better to give it time.

Rather annoying when the birthday cards get my age wrong, isn't it? I was in my forties once... got used to it by now, I suppose. But I still take it as a personal slight! Got anything on your shopping list?      Morning, love. Yes, I’ve scribbled a few things down. Strawberry jam, some good tea bags, and I wanted to buy a couple of calendar fobs too. Do you have a colour preference, or are you happy with what I pick?      Red, preferably. Those old calendars from the 80s look lovely... like something out of a school project. I remember doing art and craft with glue and feathers. Never managed to complete the turkey, mind. Still, best to left well alone. What about you?      Same, and I think I turned my hockey boots into a kaleidoscope somehow. The only thing I managed to stick up properly happened when Mr H inflating his face balloons went awry and we had to re-inflate them. Still, the memories are worth it, I suppose.      Speaking of remembering—there I was in the land of Nod last week and found a university course syllabus on sound recording. Makes you think. All those little computers we left scattered about at home?      Yes, I’ve been thinking about that too. I reckon some of those machines would be a real find in the computing museum. If I could find a screwdriver in this chaos, I’d get打包ing them up. Would you help me carry them to the museum?      Of course, I’d be happy to. I’ve had a bit of experience moving things around about. Once I volunteered at the same museum, talking to passersby about how they used to program things using punch cards. Not that I've ever done it myself, mind.      Oh, I remember those punch cards. Fascinating concept. The way computers have changed over the years is something else. I once used a computer that took up a whole room!      Yes, they've come a long way from the '70s big whirring things we used. I think you could write a whole thesis on the social history of the computer goings-on. But life improvements aside, I wonder if anyone has made a dent in the password recovery issue. Still can’t get into my old Gmail from 2003.      Oh gosh, I'm quite proud I never had that problem.

Rather annoying the new neighbours, eh? You know, the ones who've just moved in across the road. I got the distinct impression they think they're better than everyone else! Mind, I can see why they'd be proud of that new house they've got. It's a tidy little bungalow, if I do say so myself, but I do think they take   themselves   rather too seriously.      Oh, but they  do  seem lovely, Tim. I saw the lady in the garden centre the other day and was chatting to her. Didn’t even blink when I told her I'd bought a packet of onions. She just laughed and said, "Well at least you’re not buying potting soil and thinking you're a gardener!" So eccentric.      I agree with Anna, although I can see how you'd get the impression from the fence she built — nearly two metres high and doesn’t seem to be working on the front! Haha. But she was lovely at the local awards night, you remember? She won the ‘Best Newcomer’ award—voted for by the community.      I don’t know about awards. They still didn’t say hello on the walk to the shop yesterday. Mind you, we did pass them just as they were negotiating with the builder about a new cloakroom, and I suppose they were busy. Although the man didn't quite know if they were going to use a slate or quarry tile for the floor — he looked absolutely flustered.      I think they just like to appear busy, to be honest with you. Also, have either of you seen the condition their kitchen is in? I heard from Jan at the library that about half the counters are temporary — you can tell when the sun shines on them. It's like an IKEA display gone wrong.      Well, we should probably cut them some slack. Burgess says it's not unusual for people to feel a bit awkward at first when they move to a new place, especially if they haven't grown up here. After all, we all know how hard it can be to get used to a new town. Janice and I tried to do the walking group with Ann, you remember, after she moved here. She started with us once, then decided it wasn’t for her.      You’re right about that, Lesley. Although I did manage to get her to try the pub’s Sunday roast.

Rather annoying this, innit? I tried to order me some glue sticks online for the ‘obby mends... got the email saying they’re shipping now, yet still I’ve had nowt      Aye, I’ve had the same probs as well. Just like everythin’s delayed nowadays een Whitehaven. I ordered me a new laptop charger and haven’t even seen it yet      Aye, but I needed that glue stuff yesterday, so I had to go all the way to Egremont to get sommat. Sod me, it’s such a trek. You'd think the shop near here could carry basic tools and such      That’s true, and like you said, it's such a trek. I left the house this mornin' and came back in a hour, and I hadn’t even managed to buy the charger for my uni work properly      You need to do work with a dodgy charger? Blooming hell, uni! I never did sixthform or anything so I dunno what you’re bloomin’ goin’ through      Yeah I mean it's quite a lot to juggle and I'd like to have a bit of a break, but it's quite important that I stay on top of things – especiallly with the exams coming up      I imagine so. Now don’t get me wrong, I dun’ want to knock education, but I always wondered what the point was. I did one-year of uni and got my degree, but it's been so useless since—jobless as ever      I’m sorry to hear that, it must be really tough not being about to find work after all the work you put in      It is what it is. I know that I shouldn’t be laying around, but there’s not much doin’ ‘round here. There’s not even anything much on the telly that’s worth watchin’ these days      I dunno, I’ve been getting into some pretty good series as of late. They’ve been getting so much better recently, I think it's partly the tech      Tech, aye. Now that’s the bloke thing goin’ on. If I could get hold of a proper tablet or even a better specs on me phone, I could maybe get some proper remote work      That sounds like it might help, and I think I know a few people who could vouch for your skills online      Reckon that would? It would be brill if I could get back on my feet again.

Rather annoying this new house isn't it? That contractor gave us everything we wanted, but it's not like it's turned out exactly how we dreamt it would. I can't say I'm over the moon about the floorboards. They look fine, but I bet they'll creak sooner or later. Got a bit of a passive cooling system installed, you know, tried to save on the heat. Still, I reckon we'll have to think about central heating too if the winters get too cold.      Oh, and we'll be moving in for lunch soon, won't we? I made some meatballs frozen, easy enough to defrost and pop in the oven. What do you think, do you want to bring the turkey from Christmas? I remember you said left it in the back of the freezer from the big family event, and it's been sitting there for months. It might be a bit old but better than breakfast sandwiches.      Darling, I was in town at the weekend, and looked at that little second-hand shop near the bus stop. They had some real gems—vintage chairs, you know the kind that still had the occasional stain but with quite a character to them. I think we could redecorate the living area on a budget. We don’t need all new furniture. And while we’re thinking of new improvements, have you thought about the walk on the coast path this weekend? It's not far from here at all. I understand it's gorgeous at that time of year.      That walk—sounds good. I haven’t done one for ages. I remember with my son, we used to do the South West Coast Path in bits and pieces when he was a lad. He nearly about gave up on the day the bridge collapsed from the rocks above. Course, I didn’t tell my wife at the time. Not that I’d tell her now if we went out to do something like that. She hates treacherous ground.      I have no problem with it though. If anything, I love a bit of adventure. And when I was your age, my first experience was something called "Virgin Experience Days." It was great—went on a kart racing day with some friends. That's where I got the idea for travel adventures later on. Don't go wasting money on that unless you like risk though.

Rather than share a text-based conversation, I request a visual depiction of the desired format in [MIME]... What tools are available to render this as described?      You alright love? That came out a touch sharp. We were just in the middle of having a proper chat before the dishes pile up again.      Of course, sorry. Just had a brain fog moment there. This morning’s meeting spiralled me into thinking about the layout of the paper. Still trying to finalise the data analysis.      You and your spreadsheets. You made that MyUni project sound far scarier than it was. It’s just a paper, not the end of the world. Anyone I should be wary of sneaking up in the background as you present it?      I wish it were that dramatic. No, it’s just peer review, but the timeline is tight. I need to submit by the end of the week and hope for feedback. Honestly, I’m just tired. Got up at 5 again last week, reading through that bloody meta-analysis on medication adherence.      You do too much and then act like it’s mundane. Let’s have some wine and switch off for a bit. If the world ends because you didn’t finish a slide by tomorrow, someone else will publish. Promise.      Some habits are hard to break. So, what’s being poured out at the table after your colleague spoke to you at school about the new policy? You mentioned you had the talking to of the century during lunch.      Oh, it was uneventful in that it just dragged on for 20 minutes about “alignment with values” and “sustained outcomes”. As if a few bloody bullet points would fix it. Honestly, I’m starting to wonder who the real kid in the room is.      Was it Ann? Still trying to reinvent kindergarten by incorporating mindfulness mantras by 8am? I swear, if she suggests a child sit quietly in a circle meditating, I’m reinstating the mud box in the outdoor area.      Oh, it was Ann. And yes, she even mentioned it. But I had forgotten about that day over a year ago where a 5-year-old fell asleep curled up like aaurus. Probably her golden memory.      Pour us some of that Malbec, would you? before I accidentally nod off mid-conversation. I feel like I haven’t had a night off in months.

Rather annoying isn’t it, eh? You know, ever since we got that internet bill, it’s like everyone’s on our case to save more money.      Don’t I know it. I keep telling the others we’ve got to review our budget — wouldn’t do any harm. Got a meeting at work next week where we’re going to look into cutting costs. Almost as grim as the kitchen revamp I had to do last year.      If only you’d let me help with the design! I was doing a copywriting job for a designer the other week. You’d have loved the ideas they had! Not to mention the flexible work hours and the supply of tea.      Oh, bless you! But Terry here’s got this ridiculous habit of redoing the whole home on his own and I’m not the decorator. Blimey, I’ve got enough on my plate with the shift pattern at the clinic.      Blooming hell, Elaine! That’s what I said when I was working the escalator full-time and taking classes over the radio, remember? But I dug my heels in — and look at me now.      Honestly, I’ve never seen anything like it. But it does make me proud. I mean, who else would have got a commission last week for that Victorian manor up near the coast? Now  that  was a challenge!      When I first came to Rochester for training, someone at the hospital said I should’ve been a decorator. It just goes to show, doesn’t it? Also, have you seen the way the baby moves his hands — all left-handed, as if he knows better about things!      Oh! That’s something I remember from my mum. She was left-handed and that was frowned upon back in Kemsing in the '60s, believe it or not. My sister nearly broke her arm trying to write with her right hand.      Sounds like something I’d write about for the magazine column. We could run an article on that — "The Battle of the Left and Right."      Now, can we talk about food? I’m starving. This meal looks brilliant, by the way. That chicken casserole recipe of yours must be from your grandmother, Claire?      Actually, I found it online. But yes, you could say it’s in the family. We Romans always cooked together. Even with all the changes — new life, new career — some things stick around, don’t they?

Rather annoying I couldnae get through to the shops in Sunderland. I was just gonna pop ‘n get a couple o’ bits an’ bobs for dinner later. This rain's carked on me nerves, I’m tellin’ ye. Look like it’s pourin’ like a lavatory’s burst een!      Aye, puts me in mind o’ all them days on a train through Timperley. Not that side too often, me. Oh but I’ve had some interesting stories o’ train delays and the like. Once when me an’ Alice were headin’ up north... frozen to the bone even inside the carriage! Rather annoying this new coffee machine of yours, isn’t it? I tried to set it for a basic flat white last weekend and it ended up sputtering more than my own tea kettle. D’you think Labour’s leadership has the same problem—trying to fix things without really working out the basics, and then it just starts sputtering? That’s a good point, but I keep thinking maybe that’s the problem—people don’t trust where they are anymore. Whether it’s a broken coffee machine or broken promises from the government, if you don’t trust the system, you’re just not going to engage.

Rather annoying this new eligibility criteria for universal credit, isn't it? I was working full time ‘til a couple of years ago, and now I find me self down a peg with these folk who've never earned a penny in their lives.      Aye, I heard it was tightened again on the 1st of August. It was on   BBC News 12   last evening, a scandal they called it. Some policy maker in this lot, probably one of them Oxford types, thinks pulling the bread out from under people was the way to go. Looks like another mess.
