Rather annoying driving today, isn't it? That last roundabout outside Exeter was a nightmare with so much traffic. You'd think they'd build a proper motorway between Cornwall and Wales instead of endlessly trying to upgrade these A-roads.      Ah yes, motorways would be handy if it wasn't for the views, wouldn't they? Having grown up in Nantyglo, I'm a fan of A-bypasses and small roads too. At least they tell a story. Makes me think of road journey tales from my childhood, like the time me and your mum nearly got stuck in a ditch near the Severn Bridge.      That actually sounds like a decent story. You know, like that My Name is Leon type thing you mentioned to me earlier, Speaker_1, the one about the family on the move and the political tensions. I mean, you're both older, and you've been through, um… loads more political changes. What did it used to be like, you know, in the 90s or earlier?      Well, I was editing a political memoir a couple of months ago—somebody who worked with Blair during the early coalition pushes and devolution. Honestly, we’ve come a long way since then. The West was pretty proud of itself. Looking back now though, with Brexit and the mess with Wales and Scotland trying to get more independence, it feels like we’re going through a new phase.      Absolutely. Nantyglo was a mining town in my day. And you know, the Welsh political movement was massive then. Some of my best university debates were spent trying to convince politicians—prior to actually becoming one—that devolution wasn't just a fling. I remember a time when Wales having control of education or health was considered radical.      Honestly, I think younger people take it more for granted now. I grew up in Aberystwyth, so education was always passed down, you know. But with everything the UK is going through politically, it does feel intense. I’m just waiting to see how all the EU stuff plays out. My Politics 101 professor said Wales could be the next tipping point in UK politics.      That’s interesting. Wales has always had a tricky balance in the Union. But it's more than that now. With the rise of left-leaning, sustainable, green-focused movements—especially in the South Wales Valleys—it’s like the political identities are shifting.

Rather annoyingly, I've just been reading about butterfly forks. Apparently they had piercers and they had like... What was the word she used? Dressing gadgets?      I don't see how they were useful. I find it hard not to use emojis when I text anyone, really. You know what your teacher used to tell me when I was programme director? Rather annoyingly, I haven't marked all those Year 6 exams yet, and it's only a week before the weekend. James has insisted we visit his grandparents down in Cornwall. I've been over this with him, hun. Do we really want the kids fidgeting on our laps while I make my way through invigilator notes and mark schemes?      Corn-wally? That's a funny name! Is it where Dad goes fishing every year? The one with the rocks and the birds?      It was so boring last time! We just sat in the garden under the sun hat like three times, even when it stopped raining. I wanted to play on the swings!      My mum grows dahlias in the garden, and James is allergic to pollen, so I know what you mean, sweetheart. I think he just wants a chance to avoid the annual trip to Adventure Island. I've heard the new exhibition at the V&A is brilliant—boats and illuminations, and oversized clock hides, you know the kind. We could go to London instead.      Can we get adventure ice cream? The one I had in the Adventure Island book was made of cotton candy and deadly worms. At least in the book. My friend Lily says it was real.      Mate, I don’t think there’s such a thing yet, but we could try somethi—Oh, wait. Silly question. I almost forgot you can’t have dairy, Theo. They only have milk-free lattes at the V&A coffee bar, but oddly sour-dough with nut butter.      I want sour-dough! I don’t like ballet, but when we went about dollhouses there was a marble bridge and the touch wall where you could pretend to be a robot.      Noted! I'll have to check up on the new dollhouse piece they're showcasing—something interactive with rotating staircases and a cutaway of a 1930s telephone box. Sounds like fun.      I sort of miss the beach, though. I wanted to find a real seashell that wasn't on the shore—like, if the tide brought it in and then something pushed it back out.      Mummy, remember when you took us to Bournemouth and the kids at the park dressed up as pirates because of the themed holidays?      Pirates, indeed! That was before the uniforms and the Adventure Island books, wasn’t it? I had to borrow a seashell from Grace for a project—called it “Palme d’Origin,” very fancy.

: You lot, you haven't even seen what happened in history class today. Our teacher, Miss Harper—basically the only one who makes sense this year—was off! They stuck some old bloke from admin in her chair who can’t differentiate the First and Second World Wars.     : Hashtag mess! I mean, even I could get that one right! My cousin Tom actually told me a funny one last week. He swore the guy from Biology got confused and started calling glycolysis “glow-in-the-dark ooze.” I nearly.Fatalfailed the class when he said that.     : Classic! Still, I made sure I got my coursework done last night before another row with my mum. My turkey allergy is being a pain again though. She accidently gave me some dinner from the casserole, and I had to go straight to bed with an ice pack on my neck.     : Oh no! That’s rough. I used to have a dairy allergy, but I outgrew it. Honestly, the only thing I'm allergic to these days is bad weather.     : Hah, same! Speaking of, did you hear about the party at George’s place this Saturday? His parents are away, and it’s supposed to be “the most amazing – no adults – banger night of our lives.”     : Yeah! He’s already got playlists sorted and Silas is bringing the DJ gear. We might even manage to convince Rachel and someone else to come. Although she's not my biggest fan since that one time I accidentally called her hotter sister her name.     : Still, at least we get to escape school for a bit. I mean, I know I'm competing for the prefect position, but I'm so over being on the “good kid” charm train. I’d rather have fun than act like I step on eggshells for every rule.     : Mate, that’s honestly me too. I’d rather surf the weekend than study. I tried watching that new movie last night, but the trailer had me over. You seen it?     : Yeah, it was alright. Not as good as the first one, but the bike chases were epic. That reminds me, have you started your own improvements on our skatepark bike trail yet? I heard rumors you were trying to teach Alley the box jumps!     : Shawty doesn’t jump, she  leaps . Yeah, I'm working on it. Just got new grips to help me grip better, and Alley’s already bought new wheels.

Rather annoying the new roads here eh? You can’t get down that side street without it being ‘closed for... something or another’. And no one knows when they’ll properly reopen it yet.      Aye, we’ve had the same kind of nonsense in Hertfordshire. They promise eeny weeny lanes of traffic while they ‘fix the surface’ or whatever. It’s not even a proper diversion, it’s like they expect us to fly.      It’s pulling my leg. We’ve been stuck behind the same digs for weeks. Did you watch the T20s weekend? That Aaron Finch fellow is still class. I swear he’s got a bat trained to know when to whack a six.      Oh aye, he was on fire again. D’you know, I think he turned 34 last week, but still goes at it like a lad half his age. I mean, cricket... I used to live for the Ashes as a kid, you remember them days? Sitting in the garden, full pyjams on, with a big mug of tea?      Fank ye, innit. I only started getting into the limited overs properly when watching live at that trotting ground out of Tyne. The atmosphere – Mate, you could fairly feel the cheeps reverberating in your bones. You reckon bikes are gonna be as problematic as the roads? I’m looking at getting a moped, but the lassies at work are twitchy.      Aye, it's not all floring the lawns with a quad. You’ve got to be safe, make sure you’ve got the right license, and even then—poor lighting round the area can be a minefield. I had a mate who thought he was all smooth then barely noticed the handlebars were up for grabs to the bin, ‘cos he was playing up at night in Harpenden. Busted wheel, new month.      Bleedin’ ridiculous, I know. I sort of stick to my trusty bike. Though I’ve seen a bit of rust recently on the back chain whatchamacallit – you want to tell me I’m a scrap heap or can I get by with gook?      If it’s just a bit rusty, chuck in some oil and a clean gook might do the trick. But if it’s really playing up, I’d say invest in a new bike. From what I know, even a new cheapo’s worth it in the end over ruining your old rider and them fitting fees.

Okay, I’m starving and really craving Chinese food, anyone else feeling the same? We should order in tonight.      Yeah, I’m up for that! I haven’t had anything proper since lunch, and I don’t feel like cooking. What are you thinking of getting?      Mmm, passive mention of Chinese got me salivating. I’ve had this craving for sweet and sour chicken all week. I think I know that place off Old High Street; it used to be quite good last time we went.      Oh, do you mean The Golden Dragon? I remember getting frozen tofu there last time, and I can still taste it—well, I don’t think "taste" is the right word for that! Ha ha.      I’m not sure about the food, but their bubble tea is the bomb. I had it for my birthday and it definitely outshone the cake if I’m being honest.      Okay, okay, but we can’t all ordering different things. Should we just split an order or everyone order their own?      I say split an order. If we all order different things and someone forgets to pay for the delivery, we end up short by five pounds and it feels like we’re being cheated out of sushi. Remember that time at Sushi Place?      Yeah, no need to rehash that mortal sin at 8pm. Let’s just agree on the principles and then order what someone said. I’m also suspicious they might not be delivering tonight because it’s so late.      I just checked the website and they do deliver until 10pm. They’re even advertising a promotion on their biryani. I’m having the butter chicken biryani and whatever other side you want.      Okay, I'll go with the sweet and sour pork and a spring roll. Maybe we can get shared an order of sesame noodles?      I’ll take any leftover spring rolls. I’ll go with the dumplings and a small portion of General Tso’s chicken. Let’s split the sesame noodles with someone else too.      Alright, let’s finalise the order. Then someone needs to make the payment so it go through. I usually use Apple Pay.      I’ll do it, no worries. Let me go through and make sure everything is added properly. Shawarma doesn’t go in the Chinese section, though, we’d better check off the right box.

Rather annoying the new folk in next door innit? Seems they've got a budgie squawkin like it got a grievance with the local council.      Yeah, heard that! Got me kiddos runnin’ about the place like banshees, but at least it’s not eeny vocal bird passive aggression. You got the time? I reckon it’s about as productive as most a the NHS these days.      Har, har. If only. Last week I pulled a GP appointment for a cough that’s lasted months—an’ when I get there bloke looks at me like I’ve got three left lungs and says, “D’ya want a cough syrup or some vitamin C?” My lectures are far more structured!      Ten outta ten for the NHS, innit? I’ve been a nurse for fifteen years an’ it’s harder than ever. Wait times, understaffin’, paperwork—don’t get me started.      I can fathom the struggle. My sister lives in Finland, she told me they treat their healthcare like, I dunno, a human right or summat. Like a proper system with dignity and all that.      Sounds like what it used to be, from what I recollect as a girl. But now it's, like, barely stayin’ afloat. I reckon the government just sees it like a phone bill—push it toward the universities and keep the pay low. Like what someone at your level is used to!      That’s sour grapes talk—look, I came from a small town in Germany and got lucky with a university education over here, but I still have about five lectures to plan a week! Meanwhile the NHS is run by politicians with more ambition than skill.      Could barely blame ‘em if they upped and emigrated. My brother tried treslin’ for a lark to Canada last year. Said it was easier to get a decent salary and health cover there. I dunno, maybe when the kids get a bit older...      Yeah, always fantasizin’ about a new start innit? I took the kids over to Brighton once, thought it’d be like a foreign vacation. Then go back to my pond life in L8 and wonder if I shoulda braved it in Bristol or somewhere.      Aye, well. At least we’ve got fluorscopic koorge in next door for entertainment, right?      For now, ‘till it’s driven away by another yowlin’ toddler! Unless I move out and get somethin’ next to them hippies in Toxteth.

Rather annoying this new eligibility criteria eh?      Aye, it's mad if you ask me. You've got to work full-time for more than a month before they'll give you a penny. I don’t blame the young ones, I'd be frightened half to death if I was in that situation.      It's one bloody hurdle after another. My cousin in Bradford couldn’t get a job transcription because the agency would only accept candidates who'd done a full month of work   before   applying. Madness! You need the job to get the job — it's a complete catch-22.      Lakelands is no better, I'm tellin’ you. Last week they turned Myra and Elsy out of the corner store for nothin’. Probably rumour had it their DSS papers were fake.      Blimey, that’s rough. The last I heard, the police up this way are using a bit too much discretion. I pity the poor sods, you'd think they'd get a bit more support, not more hassle.      Support, what support? I got it on the telly as a lad, and I'd say it still holds — if you want something, it'd best be coming from your left hand. Ha – no respect for any of it, least not these days.      Truth be told, I've been thinking about trying to get some students from universities in Germany — we could form a co-op scheme. Bring them here for work experience, cultural exchange, and give local folks a hand with the language.      Sounds good in theory, but I wouldn't be surprised if there's a bobby on every corner now waiting for some bungle in the papers to chuck them out. I remember when they lugged Sarah and her mate out the week before Christmas. No evidence, just some bin found ‘nearby’.      A tragedy, really. And it's not as if they were any threat. I mean, I meet people from all over the world here in the market square, and I swear to God, more often than not they're better examples than the bobbies themselves.      Aye, I'd agree with that. They come here go work bin on time, if you ask me. Just give respect and get on with it. I had a Brazilian lass work in the bakery near here, Maria was her name. God rest her soul — had a heart attack two years ago after all that flour bellyache.

Rather annoying the queue at the canteen today, innit? I was starvin’ ‘n all... got to wait ‘age for a chicken pie. Blows me mind what they charge for a fookin’ salad.      Honestly! I wouldn't dream of eating in-house on a budget like mine. I always bring a sandwich. Still, it is quite something being based at a press that prints all these books—like, every language under the sun.      Honestly, it’s incredible how the press makes content accessible globally. I was reviewing the new Chinese-English dictionary the other day—it even has  yīn yuè  spelt out in Mandarin pinyin now. My postgrad taught me that!      Ten out of ten for inclusivity, I say. We’ve been working on incorporating American English variants in some of the latest grammar guides. I mean, I was born in Pennsylvania, so I definitely see both sides. It’s fascinating tracking how British and American English diverge and converge in educational publishing.      Doesn’t feel like we’re in publishing—sometimes I feel like we’re a publishing think tank. I’ve started reading up more on how language is shifting amongst younger generations. I saw a survey today saying that most kids my age use phrases like "they’re okay, but they’re not huge."      Oh, like the whole non-binary conversation. Definitely relevant in education now. We’ve had to revisit all the inclusive language policies in our reference guides.      I do wonder what our grandmums would say if they worked in here—sittin’ analysin’ dictionaries all day and not about to make a cuppa for you.      [Laughs] Honestly, you could write a whole book about that! I mean, it does sound a bit like the old proverb ‘don’t look a gift horse in the mouth.’      Speaking of gifts—has any of you ever had a publication approved as a personal project? I did once while working in Lagos. I produced a small Arabic children’s English language primer.      That’s brilliant. My grandad used to say, ‘Publish or perish.’ That was back in the 70s, obviously. He worked for one of those small education-based publishers out in York. He wrote a bloomin’ history of your basic conjugation. It was about as popular as a wet Saturday’s homework.      But that’s what we do—like, turn over rocks and find new ways of fitting language into a box... so to speak.

Rather annoying when the barista at John Lewis swears in Norwegian. I was just trying to order a flat white, and she said she wasn’t  farte  about it. I had to double-check with her that it was £2.80 and not some kind of Scandinavian satire.      That is a  bit  strange. I didn’t know we had Norwegian baristas in London cafés. I mean, I worked in one in Kingston a few years ago, but they were all from Antigua or China. Different cultures, I suppose. Funny how people just pick up bits of swearing from different places.      Yeah, I mean, learning another language is all well and good, but unless you’re living there, I don’t see the point. I tried learning French, but I gave up after a month. Made the mistake of trying to order wine with a  pas du tout  – and I still haven’t recovered.      I used to live in Paris for five years! Well, you didn’t have to study that hard once you were immersed in it. I spoke it fluently within six months. Though I still can’t pronounce  eau  without sounding like I’m choking on a frog.      You? Choking on a frog? I’m surprised – weren’t you teaching English somewhere last year? At the college in Bath?      That’s right! I taught A2 students. Bit of a culture shock, actually. I thought I’d enjoy the language part more than the teaching. But a lot of them came to class with funny ideas about the UK. One of them thought the Queen drove a Margherita bus.      I about fell over when I heard that! I mean, the Queen is quite an icon… just not in that kind of vehicle. I know I mentioned it to you before, but I still have no idea  how  someone could form that image.      I’m guessing they’ve only ever seen any ‘British’ show with exaggerated characters. I mean, I sort of get it from the outside. Downton Abbey, Doctor Who – the weirdness of the whole English monarchy must be hard to grasp.      Then again, if you told me the American president was a Harvard man who played golf and had a cat at home, I’d probably think they’re leading a quiet life, not running the most powerful country in the world. It just shows how seriously we take ourselves sometimes.

Rather chilly this morning, ain't it? I’ve just boiled the kettle and made us a pot o’ tea. You lot fancy one?      I'd murder a cup, Aunty Clara. Can I have two sugars please?       Pause Deary me, een't that sweet? I used to start the day with just a dollop of milk in me tea. Aunty Edna once swore by that too — back when we lived in Hull. Times were harder, o’ course.      Oh, don't get me started on those times — fetchin’ water, mendin’ clothes, no telly. We didn't have such luxuries in me day. I still keep me boots by the door for bursts o’ rain! I ain't trustin’ them young folk and their "weather apps."       Laughs  Well, we’re all safe and dry 'ere in Malton, Jack. And don’t mind me nonna tellin’ you ’bout Hull — the town ain’t quite the same, but I expect it still smells a bit like fish and chip shops!       Smirks  And that's what I want fer tea… Chips, salt, and vinegar?      Not too much vinegar though — gives me wind, and I’ve had enough o’ that already.       Laughs through a slight cough  Bless ‘er, at our age, wind’s just a fact o’ life. Although I reckon a bit o' plum cake might settle it. Mary, you still got that dark cherry type?      Course I do — it's in the larder about nowhere. I made a fresh batch last week. Only found it this mornin’ though, and I ain't been havin’ none myself. You're welcome to it if you lot fancies.      Honestly? I'd kill for that and more. Are the biscuits in a tin too?      Ah, now bless yeh lad — you talk such posh. You being all educated and grand knows.       Snorts  Pfft, no, you remember, I got this tutee the other day who goenvironment friendly on me and stopped me throwin’ out my crisps into the bin, said I had to separate the box and the packet.      Environment friendly? What’s that mean? Oh, I know, you mean “green”?      Yes, like that “eco” nonsense. We used to burn all our trash. I reckoned I did sommat for the planet — chemical-free burnin’ an’ all.      Oh, Mary and the environment — she always did like to be tidy. But I used to just chuck me tea bags anywhere. Still do, for that matter.

Rather annoyingly, I haven't brought anything to drink with me. I was just in such a rush to get out and see the garden before it got too dusky. This path gives such a lovely view of the city.      Look, there's a fruit stand near the gate entrance. We can go and get something from there. It was quite good last time we passed it.      Brilliant, I'm starting to get quite thirsty. I wonder what new books are on the shelves in the local library. I'm thinking of recommending some classics for the literature class.      I like to think of it mostly as a literary vacation regardless of the setting, but only if we can have some well-preserved historical buildings to wander through. I left my sunglasses back at home, the sun is getting a bit too strong for my liking.      I was about to say something similar. I've been feeling slightly sunburned. Maybe after getting a drink we could check out the library and then, you know, take a break in the shade.      I do like the way you think. After that, I can show you around a newly opened café. I think it's called 'The Good Life' - it's quite popular among both expats and local residents. They claim to have a unique blend of traditional and modern food.      That sounds perfect. I did have quite a phone call with Anna the other day. We reminisced a lot about old times. She sent us a batch of photos from our trip a few years back.      Oh, is that right? I wonder if she remembered that cafe in Barcelona where we had the most bizarre pastries I've ever tasted. I think you quite liked those insane chocolate croissants.      Yes, those were the days! I really hope she managed to photograph that place. My, time sure does fly. Speaking of which, I'd love to plan another trip with her as soon as possible. Traveling together always brought out the best in us.      As long as we can arrange to take a short break from our lunches and keep the work from consuming all our time, I'd say you're in for a nice travel buddy! I'll make sure go over my lecture notes later if you'd like.      That would be wonderful, darling. After the drink, let's head to your proposed café and then I have a few questions to ask you about one of the students in your lecture group.

So did I really just fall asleep on the tube coming back from Mia's party last night, or is that just a dream I had? I swear I’m more of a night owl, but I must have been dead tired.      Oh, you totally did — you were out cold by the time we got to your stop. I even tried nudging you saying we were there and all you did was go "Mmmh, five more minutes." Proper legend, honestly. But yeah, you were zonked. I haven't seen you like that for months.      Ugh, I can't believe I fell out of the group so quickly. All the boys were still getting another round in and everyone else was dancing like it was the last party ever. I just sort of melted into the background like a ghost. I feel dead sad about it.      Look at you, worrying about it when you probably needed your beauty sleep! Seriously, though — last night’s the first time I’ve seen you not out ordering lattes and working out at the gym all week like you usually do.      Oh, I’m not giving that up! I’ve still got my targets for the month. I just went a bit easy last night. I blame it all on Mia's mother baking – that lemon tart at the start of the night was just  too much  sweet.      Ugh, yeah, her lemon tart is like a slap to the face in the best way. Honestly, though, I’m glad you didn't stay out too late. I definitely  should  have gone to bed early, and I didn’t — I was up all night talking to Louis online because he dropped about five birthday messages after I fell asleep. Now I feel like I owe him something.      Louis again? I thought you were trying to avoid him after last semester? He just hits  too  hard with the flirty messages at 2am. And honestly, I don’t think you cope too well when he does.      Argh, I know! But he  is  being nice, and it’s not like we can't be friends! I just keep telling myself no, you don't get attached.      Yeah, go easy on it. Balance is key — like with work, exercise, boys, and, let’s face it, the boxset binges.      So true. I might seriously need a new mantra this week:  Not all who wander are lost, but some who fling themselves into every over-21 bar at 10pm definitely are.

Rather annoying the new roads here, isn't it, Vivian? I was just trying to get up to see Mary and nearly ran out of petrol on that pothole-ridden by-pass      Aye, we've had the same kind of trouble on our end in Birkenhead. I'm just hoping Mary likes peas and chips for dinner. I reckon it's about all we can afford on a Friday.      Why'd you even bring that up, Sadie? She's gonna be wanting her wine and caviar when she visits again, don't you think?      Oh, don't be silly, Ronald. We're talking about Grandmother Mary, not that My Fair Lady mistress of yours! Besides, last time she tried wine she told me it tasted like Dandelion and Burdock.      I was thinking we should do better for breakfast, though. Maybe include something a bit more... posh. Like a Full English.      You're joking about a Full English, aren't you? Water and beans, if we're lucky. Who eats proper bacon these days with minimum wage as their income?      Oh, come on, Ronald, it's not  that  bad. I earn enough –      Earns enough, eh? Funny thing is, Vivian's salary goes to making sure the whole house is run properly, while you two shirk around and never help out.      And you're just a retired maths teacher, so I wonder what you did all your life if not help out and be responsible.      Oh, you try being about forty years older and not working! I'll tell you what, I had to teach a whole class of kids yesterday because that new school barely opened and it's unstaffed.      Sadie, no one asked you to teach again. That's surprising, to say the least.      I tried to refuse, Vivian, honestly I did, but as soon as they offered me a hot meal and a proper salary I caved in! They're pathetically understaffed you know, even around this part of the country.      Well, if you've got a real income again, I expect you’ll be living it up with the champagne and chariots. Pass the peas will you?      Oh Romans, we're watching those_ratings, Ronald. You gave Fifa football a complete beating for two overtimes last night.      Sodding blamed the team for losing. My team, I might add, not the whole bloody planet!      To be fair, they lost badly last season and before that.

Rather annoying this, having the laptop play up so much. I've had to set it down on the table... got to go through some files before the weekend. Blows my mind how such a small thing can buck in.      I know what you mean, like the other night my phone wouldn't connect to my Bluetooth. It got very tedious. But at least it's easy to solve most of the time. What’s your policy on doing this stuff?      Generally, dump it to a USB drive and hope for the best. Didn’t even want to touch setting up my friend’s old Blackberry—it looked daunting. I can talk about grammar until the cows come home, but when it comes to tech, I fall flat.      Honestly, I find the water here in the South too hard for my liking. Sometimes I buy the mineral water for my tea. Got better for breakfast, no doubt.      I used to live in Kent, and I remember we used bottled water for everything. Still do, to be honest. It helps me feel like I’m treating myself, you know?      What about the bin strikes and the whole "having to hide the bins at the end of the road" silliness? That’s so much more of a task than any of this water and tech stuff.      Oh, don’t get me started. Silly little bin strikes and the mess they leave behind, and then people just chuck anything in the bags. I’ve had to pick a twig out of the bin at the corner just to get mine collected!      I still find it funny when people are surprised by the price of tap water. Voice recognition software costs less per month than my water bill now. It’s wild.      Speaking of which, have you managed to run that software properly, Speaker_1?      A little, but it just recognizes me saying the wrong words a lot. Like it once thought I was trying to program a didgeridoo. It didn’t go well.      Oh, I’ve heard of that! My niece took an interest in that instrument once, after a nice tinnie or two.      Don’t be getting antsy about glasses at your age, love. I’m 63 and I’ve got contact lenses now. Passes for a smoothie-sipping youthie if I say so myself.      Just don’t forget to sleep on them like you did over the bed when you were younger!

Rather annoying that the barista was gone when I needed an umbrella. I was just reading about SAD—Seasonal Affective Disorder—this place is so grey and I can't say I feel entirely myself.      Aw, I read somewhere that being close to birds can help with it. Got a dog friend at my farm where I used to work. I reckon his tail-wagging did more than any book I read.      I don’t have a tail-wagger to speak of, just a shelf of books and the hope for warm boots during the next shopping trip. You know I can’t abide cold feet even more than cold coffee.      Still, you’ve got the coffee here—this place definitely wins on that. I left my last student back home, a real sweetie, upset about her upcoming exams. A bit heavy for an evening in the coffee shop, but better me than her.      Ah, teacher worries—prepared all the materials, and yet you lie awake thinking if it’s enough. I know why you stay up late—your sense of responsibility, yes?      I can be a dram queen, to be fair. But teaching, it attaches to you. I sometimes wonder how much of it will stay with them. I’m at the stage where I want them to not just pass exams, but to feel something about language.      You do have a gift for it, and don’t be too hard on yourself. You've got full-time work and part-time teaching. That's already more than I can do most days.      Well, I wouldn’t be where I am without you pushing me when I started out in Bury. I remember us trying to read the English lit books and then heading out for a drink afterwards—that was fun.      Doesn't sound unappealing now that you mention it. A little drink and some warmth. Though I'd swap the weather and have me a sunny day in Cambridge any day.      Ah, but waiting till springtime? Not to rush you, but have you considered a short trip back? Family mentioned a little countryside trip—might help with the SAD and you could even help around with the dog.      Mm, that's tempting. A change of scenery and a helping hand on the farm. I suppose it could go further than an umbrella.      Exactly! And maybe I can help with the reading list too.

Rather annoying I had to cancel last minute innit, me event’s gone a bit pear-shaped ‘n I’m stuck on conference call till ten. Otherwise I’d have popped over for a bit      Aye fair enough love, the film ain’t startin’ yet anyway. I’ve bin een the kitchen sortin' chicken out, you want me to save yer some?      I only had a little something before I left work, so yeah, save me a heap would ye?      Yeah, and pass me the cologne Whilst ye’re at it innit, seems like it’s mostly rosemary and no meat tonight      You know what’s funny? Me partner, bless ‘im, though left’s a bit of a mess to be honest. D’you know how I met ‘im? We had an argument in a cafe and ‘e said I looked like a prime minister ‘cos of me blazer in!      You lot, you always looking smart. I mean, why would you wear that to a cafe?      Because I work in events and production land, as do I. I only took it off today because I was on site. Doesn’t work if you’re all scruffy in meetings      I’m not sayin it’s wrong innit. Just a bit of a shock to see someone all doused up when it could just be a mexican takeaway and some PlayStation      Honestly, I wish my dating life was just PlayStation and mexican takeaway. Been single since the end of October and I swear it’s a conspiracy – all the best people are taken or live in about five different countries      You can pass me phone number on to a few of your mates if you like love. Rather than share a specific bedtime story, I think it would do both of you good to learn a bit more about legends and stories from folklore. You both seem very interested in all this superstition      What do you mean by superstition? Is fairy bread a superstition?      Not exactly, fairy bread is a very simple tradition where if you offer slices of bread with jam on them to fairies, they would supposedly return the kindness. But superstition is more like things people believe in that have no factual basis, like the idea that you chase a wasp and it won't sting you.      Oh I like fairy bread. What is a superstition?      Just stories people tell themselves to explain things. Like the idea that if you hear the Wood Drippy, and you make a wish while you're making honey, then the wish will come true. Or the old lady that lives in the mudflats in Orford.      Oh, the old lady that helps fishermen?      Eventually yes, she helps fishermen who need it, but she might also be a quite a rude to those she doesn't like, like the time she cursed a farmer for risking her trotting horse when he got her stuck in the mud.      But, does the old lady really exist?      Well, the Sillet Stones are real, and you can see the carvings in the trees at Spilsby Wood. And there are stories of fishermen who thought they had a lucky catch, but the old woman would return and take the fish back.      But how would she know about them?      Folklore can pass down quite easily. And a lot of these stories remind people that they shouldn't take things for granted. Things like the tales of the fairies that put children to sleep forever if they passed too close to the edge of the woods.      But the fairies are good too, right? I thought they helped lost children and gave them sprite to drink out of the daffodils.      Some do, yes, but remember, even in nice stories like that, there's usually go bad fairies too. Like the ones that cut you with a needle if you tickle them, or they'll go mad and infest your barn with all sorts of queer stuff.      So, it's like those tales are supposed to make children behave to avoid being cursed or hidden away by creatures?      Exactly. These stories are all lessons to make you think, to teach kind behaviour, or to warn you about casting runes without understanding their meaning.

Rather annoying the new changes at the GP surgery, aren't they? I had to book my cough in online... What was I thinking? I nearly gave up halfway through. Rather annoying when the barista at my local café misses me a flat white and brings in a latte. I got so confused, I ended up asking for more sugar. Not a good look      Aye, we've all been there. Especially when you're running on two hours' sleep and beginning to question  everything . Heard today they 're saying Trump might actually try to make a comeback.      Ayup, sounds like a bad reality TV show. Imagine what would happen if he did! Put out the wrong policy and he'd chase it halfway round the bloomin' world with a tweet.      Can't forget the fashion, though. That pink suit and hair that looked like a doorstep sunset - you'd think he’s trying to start a firestorm from the waist up. My education was high flying, but managing that cash? Still a work in progress.      I tried to make a little profit off the side while my research takes time. Mainly doing Websites for academics trying to 'brand' their work with a mismatch of fonts and a tint of arrogance.      I told my sister to go for it on the life improvements front. If I can manage a PhD, plant-based research, and pasty connoisseuring, she can manage one new top.      Ay, fashion’s one of them things you just fall into with friends helping along the way. I saw you on Instagram yesterday, looked like Lady Macbeth went to a Sainsburys sale.

Rather annoying that the TV’s on through the wall again. Is that the one with the characters fighting?      Definitely the one with the more aggressive action sequences. I've told your mum a dozen times—watching programmes with those kinds of clips as a seven-year-old can’t be doing her any good.      I know, I know. But she adores that sort of thing. A lot worse than just the more cartoon stuff, honestly. Oh, and she was begging me to let her light her own birthday candles. You can never chase a child away from fire.      That reminds me of when I was a kid. We used to collect Blue Peter badges and everything. My uncle still has the one I made with left-over Christmas glitter. Probably worth a fortune now.      Oh, the Blue Peter badges were classic, weren’t they? I remember when I made a badge that said 'I'm a Game Show Winner' because I won five pounds in a local quiz competition. I still have it. One day, we’ll pass them over to her, maybe she’ll get a kick out of it.      She might. For now, though, she probably thinks watching shows with explosions and loud noises is just the way it is. – So, how was your lecture last night? Any interesting feedback?      It was alright. One student asked me if killer whales could kill a human while we were discussing predator-prey dynamics in marine ecosystems. Honestly, I had to check a few sources before I answered. Turns out, yes, but it's rare and largely misunderstood. They’re curious, not aggressive.      I did a lecture on social housing last week, talking about different models of squatting and how they can lead to long-term community building. One student responded with, “Is this about stealing houses?” I had to correct the whole room that squatting can involve consent and active engagement, not just the aggressive kinds of land invasion.      I know what you mean. We get such clear misconceptions. Though to be fair, when you've lived in a city like London your whole life, the concept of squatting is a foreign idea.      Exactly. Norfolks are far more rooted in rural identity and building traditions—still squat in the spirit of art collectives in the countryside, sometimes with permission from the landowners. It’s fascinating.      Like that amazing artist commune near Wymondham?

Rather annoying this new hostel they’ve set up down the street. I blame the council, always investing in flashy ideas without considering the people who live here now.      Oh, I heard about it, dear. Not sure I understand the need for it either. They’re giving it a nice name and all that—something like “The Light Shop”—but I reckon it’s not all roses. Though I suppose it’s not too bad if the old folks like us are staying in our own homes rather than ending up in those hostels.      Yeah, but don’t forget some of the old hostels were run-down and dangerous—those places weren’t fit for humans, let alone people with nowhere else to go. Just wish they’d manage them properly. I remember one back in Birmingham where the kitchen was worse than the abattoir in the back of the shop my dad used to run.      Buckshee talk! My Brian, he ran a little shop back in Costessey and we never ate takeaway, never. We made everything from scratch, and that’s how you do it, luv. I still can’t stand that processed stuff they serve in these hostels and food banks now.      You know, dear, I was looking through some old photo albums the other day—public school, wasn’t it? There’s a whole load of us from the childminder group, all at the park with the kids back in the '60s. Our John here was in one of the photos with his pupils—good teacher, he was. Funny thing was, I’d swear some of the girls in the picture ended up at the same hospital last week, all because of those flamin’ cars.      That’s right, luv. I’ve seen some of the roads that are still barely up to handle modern car traffic. You’re lucky if you don’t end up playing doctor yourself. Though I suppose it's better than the science labs I used to teach in—those smelled worse than the abattoir my colleague described once.      Oh, enough of that! What’s with people nowadays? No respect for hard work. My wife and I, we worked our backs off with our shop—every penny we got go straight back into the business if we had to.      I know, I know. And it's not that we're against progress, but you see all these new ideas and they’re never tested properly.

Rather unusual to find an academic type with a recruitment background, isn't it? I mean, they handled university lecturers and senior professionals before—straits-out different kettle of fish from what we're doing here.      Yeah, honestly, I was as surprised as you. But it was interesting how they saw the transition, you know? Kept talking about matching people to roles based on their skills, but with a more subtle, less metrics-driven approach now. I suppose working with lecturers involves a lot of trust and soft skills rather than just ticking boxes for CVs.      Ticking boxes... Right, because with lecturers it's not just about qualifications—it's about how they can convert knowledge and encourage deeper thinking. Speaking of which, did you get a chance to look at the evaluation form from Professor Woodley on academic literacy for the latest intake?      Oh yeah, and it's honestly a bit of a debate. He argues that students arriving for postgraduate studies are usually competent in discipline-specific knowledge, but their grasp of academic literacy—like critical review, argument construction—vastly differs, and it's holding them back in written assessments.      I've seen the same, especially with international students. It's not just language barriers; it's the structure of academic English, the expectations of rigour. I remember in my undergrad days, I used to write like I was telling a story, and the tutors were horrified.      Absolutely. It’s kind of funny someone who shifted from recruitment—someone used to judging resumes and experience counts—has so much insight into students who are at a different type of starting line. Still, maybe that’s the best bit, they've developed a system of peer reviews and quick literacy diagnostics. Interesting touch, especially considering this job is much less formulaic than the old one.      Yeah, and as for my thoughts, I think it’s useful—so long as it generates more discussions about how we can adapt our teaching. I'm going to suggest integrating it into my Foundation Studies module. Might streamline our support for students while keeping our academic expectations high.      That’d be great. I’ll message Professor Woodley and grab a copy of the module for you. Just make sure you keep the feedback channels open—students need to see improvements as a collaborative process.      Definitely, no point in pushing down the line if they feel it’s one size fits all.

Rather annoying this newfit military type stuff innit? Me aunt’s a bit obsessed wi’ it. She’s got them glossy mags all over the side, full o’ shiny kit an’ blokes in fatigues. My turkey still hasn’t finished cooking. Oi, is this bottle o’ red from the Cellar Vivant or was I joking? Aye, if you like the storytelling, them historical ones can get you thinking. I remember a film where some computer got so overused wi’ line-based specs they had to teach it poetry to keep it functional.      So how have you made it to your conference coordination roles after all that? Seems a strange leap from coding boxes to planning slots for conferences?

Rather annoying to be honest. He’s a bit of a doosie, if you ask me.
